evidence_items.locator: Eighty percent of firms will invest in AI during 2026, and large firms invest the most, first paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: Actual investment was far from universal among surveyed firms, including large firms. This directly contradicts the literal every-company clause without relying on adoption as a spending proxy.

A majority reporting minimal financial gains despite substantial investment supports the ordinary reading of the majority-returns clause. The same article describes a successful minority, so this does not imply that large returns were absent everywhere.

unresolved_gaps: The returns survey is not a census or a representative count of every company worldwide.
BCG's respondents may report on particular business areas rather than whole-company results, and the finding does not establish a standardized net ROI.
No supplied threshold distinguishes huge returns from smaller positive returns.
